# move — Component API

> Machine-readable API surface, generated from *.spec.ts. One section per component:
> props, allowed values, defaults, and an example. Import components from 'move'.
> 71 components. Version 0.1.54.

## Props you pass

Anything you pass a component lands on the element it renders. Three kinds settle differently:

- NAMES — aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-valuetext, title, alt. Yours wins; the component supplies a default for when you say nothing.
- HANDLERS — onClick, onKeyDown, onFocus and other DOM events. Both run, yours first. Call preventDefault() and the component stands down.
- STRUCTURE — role, type, aria-expanded, aria-sort, aria-checked, data-*. The component owns these; they say what it is and what state it is in.

For text a component displays, use its `labels` prop — one object per component.

## Accordion (disclosure)
Vertically stacked disclosure panels with single or multiple expand mode, keyboard navigation, and animated content reveal
Props:
- type: 'single' | 'multiple' (default: single) — Whether one or many items can be open at once
- value: string | string[] — Controlled value
- defaultValue: string | string[] — Default value for uncontrolled mode
- onValueChange: (value: string | string[]) => void — Called when value changes
- collapsible: boolean (default: true) — Allow closing all items in single mode
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Size affecting padding and font sizes
- variant: 'default' | 'contained' | 'ghost' (default: default) — Visual style variant
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config or false to disable
- children: React.ReactNode — Accordion items
Accordion.Root props:
- type: 'single' | 'multiple' (default: single) — Whether one or many items can be open at once
- value: string | string[] — Controlled value (string for single, string[] for multiple)
- defaultValue: string | string[] — Default value for uncontrolled mode
- onValueChange: (value: string | string[]) => void — Called when value changes
- collapsible: boolean (default: true) — Allow closing all items in single mode
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Size affecting padding and font sizes
- variant: 'default' | 'contained' | 'ghost' (default: default) — Visual style variant
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config for content expand/collapse, or false to disable
- children: React.ReactNode — Accordion items
Accordion.Item props:
- value: string — Unique identifier for this item
- children: React.ReactNode — Header and content elements
Accordion.Header props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Trigger element
Accordion.Trigger props:
- icon: React.ReactNode — Custom icon replacing the default chevron
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Hover animation config for the trigger or false to disable
- children: React.ReactNode — Trigger label text
Accordion.Content props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Expandable content
Example: <Accordion type="single" variant="default">…</Accordion>

## Alert (feedback)
Dismissible alert banner with variant colors, icon, title, and enter/exit animation
Props:
- variant: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' (default: info) — Color variant
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Alert size
- icon: string | boolean (default: true) — Icon name, true for default variant icon, false to hide
- title: React.ReactNode — Alert title
- closable: boolean (default: false) — Show close button
- onClose: () => void — Called when close button is clicked
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config or false to disable
- children: React.ReactNode — Alert description content
Example: <Alert variant="info">…</Alert>

## Align (layout)
Horizontal bar with start/center/end distribution using CSS grid
Props:
- gap: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' (default: md) — Gap between items
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' | 'baseline' (default: center) — Vertical alignment of items
- children: React.ReactNode — Align sections (Start, Center, End)
Align.Root props:
- gap: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' (default: md) — Gap between items
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' | 'baseline' (default: center) — Vertical alignment of items
- padding: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' — Padding around the bar.
- flex: boolean — Use flex (instead of grid) when you need natural-width children rather than the 1fr/auto/1fr distribution.
- fill: 'parent' | 'remaining' — Where this box's height comes from. 'parent' = all of the parent's height (the parent must be sized, and you must be its only child); 'remaining' = the space left after siblings, waiving the automatic minimum size so a scroll region below can scroll. See /systems/layout.
- children: React.ReactNode — Align sections (Start, Center, End)
Align.Start props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Start-aligned content.
Align.Center props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Centered content.
Align.End props:
- children: React.ReactNode — End-aligned content.
Example: <Align gap="md" align="center">…</Align>

## AnimatedText (typography)
Reveals text with a staggered per-character, per-word, or per-line entrance animation (anime.js splitText)
Props:
- children: React.ReactNode — The text to animate — a plain string, or (with `asChild`) a single element like `<Heading>` whose text content is split.
- as: 'span' | 'p' | 'div' | 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6' (default: span) — HTML element to render the container as. Typography is controlled by `size`/`weight`, not by the element — so the element is purely semantic.
- asChild: boolean (default: false) — Render onto the single child element (e.g. wrap a `Heading` or `Text`) via Radix Slot, instead of AnimatedText's own element — so the animated text keeps the wrapped component's typography. The child's text content is what gets split.
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' | '4xl' — Optional font size from the Move typography scale. When omitted, the text inherits its surrounding typography (no data-size, no override).
- weight: 'normal' | 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold' — Optional font weight from the Move typography scale. When omitted, the text inherits its surrounding weight (no data-weight, no override).
- by: 'character' | 'word' | 'line' (default: word) — Granularity the text is split into before staggering
- effect: 'fade' | 'slideUp' | 'blurUp' | 'scale' (default: fade) — Per-segment entrance animation
- trigger: 'mount' | 'inView' | 'hover' (default: inView) — When the reveal runs: immediately on mount, when scrolled into view (IntersectionObserver), or on pointer hover
- once: boolean (default: true) — For inView/hover triggers, animate only the first time (do not re-run on re-entry)
- stagger: number (default: null) — Delay in ms between segments. When null, a sensible per-`by` default is used (~30 character / 60 word / 120 line).
- delay: number (default: 0) — Delay in ms before the first segment animates
- duration: number (default: 600) — Duration in ms of each segment animation
- nowrap: boolean (default: false) — Keep the text on a single line (white-space: nowrap) instead of wrapping. When false (default) long text wraps naturally (white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: break-word).
Example: <AnimatedText as="span" weight="normal">…</AnimatedText>

## AudioPlayer (media)
Horizontal bar-style audio player with play/pause, progress scrubbing, volume control, subtitle overlay, playback speed, and settings menu
Props:
- src: string — Audio source URL
- autoPlay: boolean — Start playback automatically
- muted: boolean — Start muted
- loop: boolean — Loop playback
- playbackRate: number — Controlled playback speed
- onPlaybackRateChange: (rate: number) => void — Called when playback rate changes
- playing: boolean — Controlled playing state
- onPlayingChange: (playing: boolean) => void — Called when playing state changes
- volume: number — Controlled volume (0-1)
- onVolumeChange: (volume: number) => void — Called when volume changes
- currentTime: number — Controlled current playback time in seconds
- onTimeChange: (time: number) => void — Called when current time changes
- onEnded: () => void — Called when playback ends
- onError: (error: MediaError | null) => void — Called on playback error
- onReady: () => void — Called when audio metadata is loaded and ready
- subtitles: SubtitleTrack[] — Array of subtitle/caption tracks (VTT files)
- qualities: QualityOption[] — Array of quality options for source switching
- audioTracks: AudioTrack[] — Array of audio track options for source switching
- onQualityChange: (quality: QualityOption) => void — Called when quality is changed
- onAudioTrackChange: (track: AudioTrack) => void — Called when audio track is changed
- showSettings: boolean (default: true) — Show the settings menu button
- showSubtitles: boolean (default: true) — Show the subtitles toggle button (only if subtitles are provided)
- showVolume: boolean (default: true) — Show volume button and slider
- showTime: boolean (default: true) — Show the time display
- labels: Partial<AudioPlayerLabels> — i18n labels for the player controls
- radius: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' (default: none) — Border radius of the player container
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Size variant controlling padding, gap, and control button dimensions
- children: React.ReactNode — Additional content rendered inside the player container
Example: <AudioPlayer radius="none">…</AudioPlayer>

## Autocomplete (forms)
Searchable dropdown with single/multi-value support, tag management, keyboard navigation, and filtered option list
Autocomplete.Root props:
- value: string | string[] — Controlled selected value(s)
- defaultValue: string | string[] — Default selected value(s) (uncontrolled)
- onValueChange: (value: string | string[]) => void — Called when selected value changes
- open: boolean — Controlled open state
- defaultOpen: boolean (default: false) — Default open state (uncontrolled)
- onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void — Called when open state changes
- multiple: boolean (default: false) — Enable multi-select with tags
- inputValue: string — Controlled input text value
- defaultInputValue: string (default: ) — Default input text (uncontrolled)
- onInputValueChange: (value: string) => void — Called when input text changes
- loading: boolean (default: false) — Show loading state in content
- resource: AsyncResource<unknown> — Async data source driving loading/error state for the options list (supersedes loading; feeds RetryTrigger)
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config for popup enter/exit
- closeOnSelect: boolean — Close popup after selection (defaults to true for single, false for multiple)
- openOnFocus: boolean (default: true) — Open popup when input receives focus
- allowCustomValue: boolean (default: false) — Allow input value that does not match any item
- filterFn: (inputValue: string, itemValue: string, itemLabel: string) => boolean — Custom filter function for items
- labels: Partial<AutocompleteLabels> — Accessible label overrides (clearAll, removeTag, retry)
- children: React.ReactNode — Autocomplete sub-components
Autocomplete.Trigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Input, TagList, Icon, ClearTrigger
- disabled: boolean — Disabled state
- invalid: boolean — Invalid state
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Trigger size
- variant: 'outlined' | 'filled' (default: outlined) — Trigger variant
- width: 'auto' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' (default: full) — How wide the trigger is, from the field-width scale. Steps are sized in ch for the content each expects, and every one is capped at the space available. 'full' takes the column.
Autocomplete.Input props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- placeholder: string — Input placeholder text
- disabled: boolean — Disabled state
Autocomplete.TagList props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom tag elements or auto-generated
Autocomplete.Tag props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Tag label content
- value: string — Value this tag represents
Autocomplete.Icon props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom icon content
Autocomplete.ClearTrigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom icon content
Autocomplete.Content props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Items, groups, empty, loading
- sideOffset: number (default: 4) — Offset from trigger
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' (default: start) — Alignment relative to trigger
- container: HTMLElement — Custom portal mount target. Defaults to document.body.
- width: 'anchor' | 'content' (default: anchor) — Where the popover takes its width from. 'anchor' matches the trigger, so field and list read as one control; 'content' sizes to the widest option — what a narrow field with long labels needs — and stays inside the room the anchor has.
- minWidth: Dimension — Minimum popover width.
- maxWidth: Dimension — Maximum popover width.
Autocomplete.Item props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Item label content
- value: string — Item value for selection
- label: string — Text label for filtering (extracted from children if omitted)
- disabled: boolean — Disabled state
Autocomplete.ItemIndicator props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom indicator icon
Autocomplete.Group props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — GroupLabel and items
Autocomplete.GroupLabel props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Label text
Autocomplete.Empty props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Empty message content
Autocomplete.Loading props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Loading indicator content
Autocomplete.Error props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Error message content
Autocomplete.RetryTrigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Retry button content
Autocomplete.Separator props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
Example: <Autocomplete.Root>…</Autocomplete.Root>

## Avatar (data-display)
User avatar with image, fallback, and size options

- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' (default: md) — Avatar size
- color: 'gray' | 'red' | 'pink' | 'grape' | 'violet' | 'indigo' | 'blue' | 'cyan' | 'teal' | 'green' | 'lime' | 'yellow' | 'orange' — Tints the fallback bg/fg using the named Open Color palette.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Optional declarative animation config — none by default (the mount fade is CSS)
- children: React.ReactNode — Avatar.Image and Avatar.Fallback
Avatar.Image props:
- src: string — Image source URL
- alt: string — Image alt text
- onLoadingStatusChange: (status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'loaded' | 'error') => void — Loading status callback
Avatar.Fallback props:
- delayMs: number — Delay before showing fallback
- children: React.ReactNode — Fallback content (initials, icon)
Example: <Avatar.Root>…</Avatar.Root>

## Breadcrumb (navigation)
Navigation breadcrumb trail with auto-injected separators, collapsible overflow with ellipsis, and customizable separator content
Props:
- separator: React.ReactNode — Custom separator content
- maxItems: number — Maximum visible items before collapsing
- itemsBeforeCollapse: number (default: 1) — Items shown before ellipsis
- itemsAfterCollapse: number (default: 1) — Items shown after ellipsis
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Breadcrumb size
- labels: Partial<BreadcrumbLabels> — Overridable user-facing strings
- children: React.ReactNode — Breadcrumb.Item children
Breadcrumb.Root props:
- separator: React.ReactNode — Custom separator content (defaults to chevron-right icon)
- maxItems: number — Maximum visible items before collapsing with ellipsis
- itemsBeforeCollapse: number (default: 1) — Number of items to show before ellipsis when collapsed
- itemsAfterCollapse: number (default: 1) — Number of items to show after ellipsis when collapsed
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Breadcrumb size affecting font size and gap
- labels: Partial<BreadcrumbLabels> — Overridable user-facing strings
- children: React.ReactNode — Breadcrumb.Item children
Breadcrumb.Item props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Item content (Link or Page)
Breadcrumb.Link props:
- asChild: boolean (default: false) — Render as Slot to merge props onto child element (e.g. router Link)
- children: React.ReactNode — Link content
Breadcrumb.Page props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Current page text
Breadcrumb.Separator props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom separator content (falls back to context separator)
Breadcrumb.Ellipsis props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom ellipsis content (defaults to horizontal ellipsis character)
Example: <Breadcrumb>…</Breadcrumb>

## Button (actions)
Clickable interactive element with variant, size, and animation support
Props:
- variant: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'danger' (default: primary) — Visual style variant
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Button size
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config for hover/press interactions
- asChild: boolean (default: false) — Render as child element via Radix Slot
- fullWidth: boolean — Stretch the button to fill its container width — for form submit actions, sidebar rows, and other full-width contexts.
- type: string (default: button) — HTML button type attribute
- disabled: boolean (default: false) — Disabled state
- children: React.ReactNode — Button content
Button.Group props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Button children
Example: <Button variant="primary">…</Button>

## Calendar (date-time)
Date selection grid supporting single, range, and multiple selection modes with event display, keyboard navigation, and locale-aware formatting
Calendar.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Calendar.Nav and Calendar.Grid (and any custom composition)
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- mode: SelectionMode (default: single) — Selection mode: single date, date range, or multiple dates
- value: Date | DateRange | Date[] | null — Controlled selected value (shape depends on mode)
- defaultValue: Date | DateRange | Date[] | null — Initial selected value when uncontrolled
- onValueChange: (value: any) => void — Called when the selection changes
- events: CalendarEvent[] (default: []) — List of events to display on day cells
- locale: string (default: en-US) — BCP-47 locale tag for date formatting and weekday order
- weekStartsOn: number — First day of week (0=Sunday, 1=Monday); defaults from locale
- constraints: CalendarConstraints — Min/max date and disabled-day predicate
- numberOfMonths: number (default: 1) — Number of months to render side-by-side
- showWeekNumbers: boolean (default: false) — Show ISO week number column on each grid
- yearRange: number (default: 12) — Number of years on either side of the current year shown in the year picker
- fixedWeeks: boolean (default: false) — Always render six week rows so the grid does not reflow as months change
- renderDayCell: RenderDayCell — Custom renderer for day cell content
- renderEvent: RenderEvent — Custom renderer for an event chip inside a day cell
- labels: CalendarLabels — Localizable strings for nav buttons and pickers
Calendar.Nav props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- sp: CalendarNavSp — Slot-prop overrides for the nav’s previous/next buttons, forwarded to the shared CalendarNav
Calendar.Grid props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- sp: MonthGridSp — Slot-prop overrides for the grid, weekday header row and cells, week rows and the week-number gutter, forwarded to the shared MonthGrid
Example: <Calendar.Root>…</Calendar.Root>

## CalendarView (date-time)
Full-featured calendar view supporting day, week, month, and agenda modes with event display, time grid, locale-aware formatting, and view switching
CalendarView.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — CalendarView.Header and CalendarView.Body composition
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- view: CalendarViewMode — Controlled current view (day | week | month | agenda)
- defaultView: CalendarViewMode (default: month) — Initial view when uncontrolled
- onViewChange: (view: CalendarViewMode) => void — Called when the view changes
- date: Date — Controlled focus date driving the displayed range
- defaultDate: Date (default: new Date()) — Initial focus date when uncontrolled
- onDateChange: (date: Date) => void — Called when the focus date changes
- events: CalendarEvent[] (default: []) — List of events to display across views
- locale: string (default: en-US) — BCP-47 locale tag for date and time formatting
- weekStartsOn: number — First day of week (0=Sunday, 1=Monday); defaults from locale
- startHour: number (default: 0) — First hour shown in day/week time grid (0-23)
- endHour: number (default: 24) — Last hour shown in day/week time grid (1-24)
- slotHeight: string — CSS height for each time slot row in the day/week time grid
- slotInterval: 30 | 60 (default: 60) — Time slot granularity in minutes
- maxEventsPerCell: number (default: 3) — Maximum visible events per month cell before overflow popover
- renderEvent: RenderEvent — Custom renderer for an event chip
- onEventClick: (event: CalendarEvent, e: React.MouseEvent) => void — Called when an event chip is clicked
- onSlotClick: (date: Date, e: React.MouseEvent) => void — Called when an empty time slot is clicked (day/week views)
- onDayClick: (date: Date, e: React.MouseEvent) => void — Called when a day cell is clicked (month view); navigates to day view by default
- onAllDayClick: (date: Date, e: React.MouseEvent) => void — Called when an empty all-day slot is clicked (day/week views)
- showAllDay: boolean (default: false) — Always show the all-day section in day/week views
- labels: CalendarViewLabels — Localizable strings for nav, today, view switcher, all-day, empty agenda, and overflow
CalendarView.Header props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Header composition (Nav, Title, Today, ViewSwitcher)
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
CalendarView.Nav props:
- className: string — CSS class name
CalendarView.Title props:
- className: string — CSS class name
CalendarView.Today props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom button label; defaults to labels.today
- className: string — CSS class name
CalendarView.ViewSwitcher props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- views: CalendarViewMode[] (default: ['day', 'week', 'month', 'agenda']) — Subset of views to expose in the switcher
CalendarView.Body props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
Example: <CalendarView.Root>…</CalendarView.Root>

## Carousel (media)
Compound scroll-snap carousel with configurable orientation, slides-per-view, autoplay, drag/swipe, and built-in trigger/indicator controls
Carousel.Root props:
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' (default: horizontal) — Scroll orientation
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' (default: start) — Snap alignment for slides
- slidesPerView: number (default: 1) — Number of slides visible at once
- loop: boolean (default: false) — Loop back to start after last slide
- autoplay: number (default: 0) — Auto-advance interval in ms (0 = off)
- draggable: boolean (default: true) — Allow drag/swipe navigation
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Slide transition animation config
- page: number — Controlled active page (0-indexed)
- defaultPage: number — Initial page when uncontrolled
- onPageChange: (page: number) => void — Called when active page changes
- showTriggers: boolean (default: false) — Render built-in prev/next trigger buttons
- showIndicators: boolean (default: false) — Render built-in page indicator dots
- triggerPlacement: 'none' | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'overlay' | 'indicator-sides' (default: top) — Placement strategy for built-in triggers
- triggerAlign: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' (default: end) — Alignment for trigger row and indicator-sides layout
- triggerSize: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Size of built-in trigger buttons
- triggerVariant: 'surface' | 'ghost' | 'solid' (default: surface) — Visual variant for built-in trigger buttons
- overlayInset: string | number (default: var(--move-spacing-sm)) — Horizontal inset for overlay trigger placement
- overlayOffsetY: string | number (default: 50%) — Vertical offset for overlay trigger placement
- overlayHideUntilHover: boolean (default: false) — Hide overlay triggers until hover/focus
- indicatorPlacement: 'inside-bottom' | 'below' (default: below) — Placement for built-in indicators
- indicatorGap: string | number — Override indicator gap token
- indicatorInset: string | number (default: var(--move-spacing-sm)) — Horizontal inset for inside-bottom indicators
- children: React.ReactNode — Carousel sub-components (Viewport, IndicatorGroup, etc.)
Carousel.Viewport props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Slide components
Carousel.Slide props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Slide content
Carousel.PrevTrigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom trigger content (default: chevron icon)
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' — Button size
- variant: 'surface' | 'ghost' | 'solid' — Button visual variant
Carousel.NextTrigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom trigger content (default: chevron icon)
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' — Button size
- variant: 'surface' | 'ghost' | 'solid' — Button visual variant
Carousel.IndicatorGroup props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom indicators (auto-generated if omitted)
Carousel.Indicator props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom indicator content
- index: number — The page index this indicator targets
Example: <Carousel.Root orientation="horizontal" align="start">…</Carousel.Root>

## Chart (data-display)
Token-aware chart shell. Owns the frame, scales, accessible name, data-table alternative, legend, tooltip, hover emphasis and async status; delegates drawing to a swappable renderer. The built-in renderer is Move-owned React SVG over its own scale and path maths, so the package takes on no charting dependency; libraries plug in as optional adapters. Covers line, area, bar and scatter over a shared axis (category or linear x, three interpolations, stacking, reference lines, and `axes={false}` for a sparkline), plus pie and donut, which share none of that machinery and take their own path.
Props:
- data: readonly Record<string, unknown>[] — Row-oriented source data. One object per x position.
- x: string — Key in each row holding the x/category value.
- series: ChartSeries[] — One entry per drawn series: { key, type, label?, color?, axis?, dash? }. Order fixes draw order and legend order.
- caption: string — Chart title. Renders as the figcaption and supplies the accessible name — required, because a chart without one is unusable non-visually. Named `caption` rather than `title` so it cannot collide with the HTML title attribute.
- hideCaption: boolean (default: false) — Visually hide the caption while keeping it in the accessibility tree.
- summary: string (default: null) — Optional one-line trend summary announced before the data table. When absent the shell derives one from the series (first/last value and direction).
- renderer: ChartRenderer (default: null) — Swap the drawing layer for a charting library. Falls back to the built-in SVG renderer when omitted.
- resource: AsyncResource<unknown> (default: null) — Async source status. Drives the loading, error, retry, and empty states so they are shell-owned rather than per-renderer.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Scales tick font size, stroke width, point radius, and tick density.
- grid: 'none' | 'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'both' (default: horizontal) — Which grid lines the renderer draws.
- legend: boolean (default: true) — Render the series legend below the plot.
- tooltip: boolean (default: true) — Show every series' value at the hovered position. Rendered by the shell over the plot, so it looks and behaves the same for any renderer that reports its plot rect.
- dots: boolean (default: false) — Mark each data point on line and area series.
- rules: ChartRule[] (default: null) — Reference lines across the plot — a target, a budget, an SLA, an average. Annotations rather than series: they carry no data of their own, they give the data something to be read against. A rule extends the value domain, so a target above everything achieved still appears. Ignored by a pie, which has no value axis.
- axes: boolean (default: true) — Draw the tick labels and baseline. Off makes a sparkline: the margins collapse with them, so the drawing fills the box. Pair with grid="none", legend={false} and tooltip={false}.
- innerRadius: number (default: 0) — Hole size for a pie, as a fraction of the radius. 0 is a full pie, around 0.6 reads as a donut. Ignored by every other series type.
- xScale: 'category' | 'linear' (default: category) — How x positions are derived. `category` spaces rows evenly by index; `linear` places each at its own numeric x, which is what unevenly sampled or time-series data needs — a category axis would draw equal gaps between unequal intervals. Timestamps are numbers: pass epoch milliseconds and a `formatX`. Falls back to `category` if any x value is not finite.
- curve: 'linear' | 'monotone' | 'step' (default: linear) — How line and area paths travel between points. `monotone` smooths without inventing peaks the data does not contain.
- stacked: boolean (default: false) — Stack bar and area series sharing an axis instead of overlaying them.
- aspect: number (default: 2) — Width-to-height ratio for the viewport. Ignored when `height` is set.
- height: number | string (default: null) — Explicit plot height. Overrides `aspect` when set.
- palette: Color[] (default: null) — Override the categorical series ramp with Move color names. Defaults to the theme-derived ramp.
- formatX: (value: unknown) => string (default: null) — Format x tick labels and the data-table header column.
- formatY: (value: number) => string (default: null) — Format y tick labels, data-table cells, and the derived summary.
- dataTable: boolean | number (default: true) — Render the visually hidden data table. A number sets the row count past which the table is dropped and the summary carries the chart alone (200 by default, following Highcharts, which stops exposing individual points at the same count). Turn it off outright only when an equivalent table is already on the page.
- labels: Partial<ChartLabels> (default: null) — Override the built-in user-facing strings.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false (default: null) — Override or disable the series entrance animation.
- entranceThreshold: number | 'always' (default: 0.8) — How much of the chart must be on screen before the entrance plays, as a fraction of its own height. 'always' drops the visibility gate and plays as soon as the chart can draw. The ask is capped against what the chart can actually reach, since one taller than the viewport can never satisfy a high fraction.
Example: <Chart grid="horizontal" xScale="category">…</Chart>

## ColorInput (forms)
Form input with color preview swatch that opens a ColorPicker popover, supporting multiple color formats and eye dropper
Props:
- variant: 'outlined' | 'filled' (default: outlined) — Input variant
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Input size
- width: 'auto' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' (default: full) — How wide the field is, from the field-width scale. Steps are sized in ch for the content each expects, and every one is capped at the space available. 'full' takes the column, 'auto' hugs the content.
- format: ColorFormat (default: hex) — Active color format (hex, hexa, rgb, rgba, hsl, hsla)
- value: string — Controlled color value
- defaultValue: string — Default color value (uncontrolled)
- onValueChange: (value: string) => void — Called on every color change (during drag)
- onChangeEnd: (value: string) => void — Called when interaction ends (drag release, blur)
- onFormatChange: (format: ColorFormat) => void — Called when format changes in picker
- formatOptions: BaseColorFormat[] — Available base formats in picker selector
- swatches: string[] — Preset color swatches in picker
- swatchesPerRow: number (default: 7) — Number of swatches per row
- withPicker: boolean (default: true) — Show saturation/hue/alpha picker area
- withEyeDropper: boolean — Show eye dropper button (browser support required)
- closeOnColorSwatchClick: boolean (default: true) — Close popover after swatch click in picker
- invalid: boolean — Invalid state
- disabled: boolean — Disabled state
- readOnly: boolean — Read-only state
- placeholder: string — Input placeholder text
- name: string — Form field name
- id: string — Input element id
- required: boolean — Required state
- autoFocus: boolean — Auto-focus on mount
- onFocus: React.FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> — Input focus handler
- onBlur: React.FocusEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> — Input blur handler
- labels: Partial<ColorInputLabels> — Accessible label overrides
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
Example: <ColorInput variant="outlined" width="full">…</ColorInput>

## FileUpload (forms)
Compound file upload component with drag-and-drop dropzone, file list management, progress tracking, and pluggable upload adapter system
FileUpload.Root props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Sub-components (Dropzone, Trigger, ItemGroup, etc.)
- accept: string | string[] — Accepted file types — MIME types, extensions, or wildcards
- maxSize: number — Maximum file size in bytes
- maxFiles: number — Maximum number of files
- multiple: boolean (default: true) — Allow multiple file selection
- disabled: boolean — Disabled state
- value: File[] — Controlled file list
- defaultValue: File[] — Default file list (uncontrolled)
- onFilesChange: (files: File[]) => void — Called when the file list changes
- onFileReject: (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void — Called when files fail validation
- validate: (file: File) => string | null — Custom per-file validation function
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Component size
- variant: 'default' | 'compact' (default: default) — Layout variant
- adapter: FileUploadAdapter — Upload adapter function for server uploads
- autoUpload: boolean (default: false) — Automatically start uploading when files are added
- concurrency: number (default: 3) — Maximum concurrent uploads
- onUploadComplete: (entry: FileUploadEntry) => void — Called when a single file upload completes
- onUploadError: (entry: FileUploadEntry, error: Error) => void — Called when a single file upload fails
- onAllComplete: (entries: FileUploadEntry[]) => void — Called when all files have finished uploading
- labels: Partial<FileUploadLabels> — Overridable user-facing strings
- removeOnComplete: boolean | number — Remove files from list after upload completes; true = 2000ms delay, number = custom delay in ms
FileUpload.Dropzone props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Dropzone content (instructions, icon, etc.)
FileUpload.Trigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Trigger content (e.g. Button)

- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Item components
FileUpload.Item props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Item contents (Preview, Name, Size, Delete, etc.)
- file: File — The File object this item represents

- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom fallback icon for non-image files

- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles

- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles

- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom delete icon (defaults to X icon). Localize the default "Remove {filename}" announcement via the Root labels prop.
FileUpload.ClearTrigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Trigger content (e.g. Button)

## Grid (layout)
CSS grid layout container with equal-column, span-based, and auto-fit modes plus a Cell sub-component for placement control
Props:
- cols: number — Equal-width columns (shorthand for repeat(N, 1fr))
- rows: number — Equal-height rows (shorthand for repeat(N, 1fr))
- columns: number — Total columns for span-based mode (default 12)
- minChildWidth: string — Auto-fit: minimum child width before wrapping (e.g. "200px")
- gap: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' (default: md) — Gap between grid items
- rowGap: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' — Row gap override
- columnGap: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' — Column gap override
- padding: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' — Inner padding around grid content
- collapseBelow: string — Container width (px) below which grid collapses to 1 column
- stagger: boolean | { delay?: number; from?: 'first' | 'last' | 'center' } (default: false) — Opt-in: reveal direct children with a staggered fade+rise entrance on mount. `true` uses defaults (60ms between items, from first); pass an object to tune `delay`/`from`. Off by default. Disable or override via the `animations` prop. (Replaces the former ImageGroup gallery component — use `<Grid stagger>` with `Image` children.)
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Override or disable the entrance stagger animation (only relevant when `stagger` is set).
- children: React.ReactNode — Grid.Cell children
Grid.Cell props:
- span: number — Column span
- rowSpan: number — Row span
- offset: number — Columns to skip before this cell
- order: number — Visual order
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' — Self-alignment within the grid cell
- children: React.ReactNode — Cell content
Example: <Grid gap="md" rowGap="xs">…</Grid>

## Heading (typography)
Semantic heading element (h1-h6) with weight, color, tracking, alignment, and truncation control

- weight: 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold' — Font weight
- color: 'base' | 'muted' | 'subtle' (default: base) — Text color
- tracking: 'tight' | 'normal' (default: tight) — Letter spacing
- align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' — Text alignment (only set when provided)
- truncate: Truncate — Truncate overflowing text: true/'end', 'start', or 'clamp'
- lines: number — Max lines for truncate='clamp' (default 2)
- tooltip: boolean — With truncate, show full text in a tooltip when actually cut off
- readableWidth: boolean — Cap the line length to a comfortable reading measure (WCAG 1.4.8) — for a standalone heading/paragraph; use Prose for real long-form content
- className: string — Additional CSS class
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Heading text content

## Image (media)
Responsive image wrapper with object-fit, radius, aspect ratio, fallback state, and action overlay support
Props:
- src: string — Image source URL
- sources: ImageSource[] — Array of responsive image variants with intrinsic pixel widths for container-based resolution
- alt: string — Alt text for the image
- fallbackSrc: string — Fallback image URL displayed when the primary src fails
- fit: 'cover' | 'contain' | 'fill' | 'none' | 'scale-down' (default: cover) — CSS object-fit value for the img element
- backdrop: boolean (default: false) — Fill letterbox bands with a blurred, scaled-up copy of the image behind it (the Apple Music / Spotify pattern). Most useful with `fit="contain"` on mixed aspect ratios; off by default.
- radius: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' (default: none) — Border radius applied to the root container
- position: 'center' | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'top left' | 'top right' | 'bottom left' | 'bottom right' (default: center) — CSS object-position value for the img element
- aspectRatio: string — CSS aspect-ratio value applied to the root container
- width: Dimension — Width of the root container (number treated as px)
- height: Dimension — Height of the root container (number treated as px)
- loading: 'lazy' | 'eager' — Native loading attribute passed to the img element
- action: React.ReactNode — Content rendered in the action overlay, revealed on hover or focus.
- interactive: boolean — Make the image a click target. Adds cursor, hover tint, focus ring, and Enter/Space activation. Defaults to true when `onClick` is set.
- onClick: (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => void — Click handler on the wrapper.
- onLoad: React.ReactEventHandler<HTMLImageElement> — Called when the image loads successfully
- onError: React.ReactEventHandler<HTMLImageElement> — Called when the image fails to load
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom fallback content rendered inside the fallback slot when image errors and no fallbackSrc is set
Example: <Image fit="cover" radius="none">…</Image>

## LayoutGroup (layout)
Container that FLIP-animates its direct children to their new positions when the set or order changes (filter, sort, reorder, add, remove)
Props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Items to lay out. Each needs a stable React key so the FLIP engine can track it across reorders.
- as: 'div' | 'ul' | 'ol' | 'section' (default: div) — Semantic container element to render.
- asChild: boolean (default: false) — Render onto the single child element (e.g. wrap a `Stack` or `Grid`) via Radix Slot, so that component provides the layout while LayoutGroup FLIP-animates its children. The wrapped element becomes the tracked container.
- enter: 'fade' | 'scale' | 'fade-scale' | 'none' (default: fade-scale) — Entrance animation for newly added children.
- exit: 'fade' | 'scale' | 'fade-scale' | 'none' (default: fade-scale) — Exit animation for removed children (the node is briefly retained to animate out, then unmounted).
- duration: number (default: 350) — Duration in ms of the position move and enter/exit animations.
- stagger: number (default: 0) — Delay in ms between children for the one-time `initial` mount reveal. Ongoing changes (moves, entrances, exits) stay synchronized so filtering reads as one coherent reflow rather than a top-to-bottom cascade. 0 disables staggering.
- initial: boolean (default: false) — Also play the enter animation (staggered) for the children present at mount — a one-time entrance reveal on load.
- disabled: boolean (default: false) — Opt out of animation — children jump straight to their final layout. Also implied by prefers-reduced-motion.
- className: string — Class applied to the root.
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline style applied to the root.
Example: <LayoutGroup as="div" enter="fade-scale">…</LayoutGroup>

- underline: 'always' | 'hover' | 'none' (default: always) — Underline behavior
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'lg' | 'xl' — Font size (optional, inherits when unset)
- external: boolean — Opens in new tab with noopener noreferrer
- asChild: boolean (default: false) — Render as child element via Radix Slot
- truncate: Truncate — Truncate overflowing text: true/'end', 'start', or 'clamp'
- lines: number — Max lines for truncate='clamp' (default 2)
- tooltip: boolean — With truncate, show full text in a tooltip when actually cut off
- children: React.ReactNode — Link content
Example: <Link variant="default" underline="always">…</Link>

- active: boolean (default: false) — Visual active/selected state
- disabled: boolean (default: false) — Dims item and prevents interaction
- children: React.ReactNode — Leading, Content, Trailing, or Meta children
List.Leading props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Avatar, icon, checkbox, or other leading visual
List.Content props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Title, Description, and any additional content

- truncate: Truncate (default: end) — How the title truncates when it overflows (default 'end'; 'middle' for paths)
- lines: number — Max lines for truncate='clamp'
- children: React.ReactNode — Primary text content
List.Description props:
- lines: 1 | 2 | 3 | 'none' (default: none) — Number of visible lines before truncation (line-clamp). Defaults to none — opt into truncation explicitly.

List.Trailing props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Badge, button, timestamp, menu, or other trailing content

## MarkerList (data-display)
Nested marker list (semantic ul/ol) with a bullet, number, or icon marker per item, per-level markers that nested lists inherit by depth, and controllable indent — the marker-list family, distinct from the item-oriented ItemList
Props:
- ordered: boolean (default: false) — Ordered <ol> vs unordered <ul>.
- marker: 'disc' | 'circle' | 'square' | 'decimal' | 'alpha' | 'roman' (default: null) — Marker style for this level (null derives disc/decimal from ordered).
- markers: ('disc' | 'circle' | 'square' | 'decimal' | 'alpha' | 'roman')[] — Per-depth marker styles, inherited by nested lists.
- icon: string (default: null) — Icon marker (by name) for all items at this level.
- spacing: 'none' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: xs) — Vertical gap between items.
- indent: 'none' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Indentation per nested level.
- center: boolean (default: false) — Vertically center the marker (default: align to first line).
- children: React.ReactNode — MarkerList.Item children.
MarkerList.Root props:
- ordered: boolean (default: false) — Render an ordered <ol> (numbered) instead of an unordered <ul> (bulleted).
- marker: 'disc' | 'circle' | 'square' | 'decimal' | 'alpha' | 'roman' (default: null) — Marker style for this level. Bullets (disc/circle/square) for unordered, numbering (decimal/alpha/roman) for ordered. When null, derives disc (unordered) or decimal (ordered).
- markers: ('disc' | 'circle' | 'square' | 'decimal' | 'alpha' | 'roman')[] — Per-depth marker styles (level 0, 1, 2…). Provided on the root and inherited via context by every nested MarkerList, which picks the entry for its own depth. `marker` overrides for a single level.
- icon: string (default: null) — Use a resolved Icon (by name) as the marker for every item at this level, instead of a bullet/number. Overridable per item.
- spacing: 'none' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: xs) — Vertical gap between items.
- indent: 'none' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Indentation added per nested level.
- center: boolean (default: false) — Vertically center each marker to its item. Default aligns the marker to the first line (correct for multi-line items).
- children: React.ReactNode — MarkerList.Item children.
MarkerList.Item props:
- marker: 'disc' | 'circle' | 'square' | 'decimal' | 'alpha' | 'roman' (default: null) — Override this item's marker style.
- icon: string (default: null) — Override this item's marker with a resolved Icon (by name).
- children: React.ReactNode — Item content, and optionally a nested MarkerList.
Example: <MarkerList marker="null" spacing="xs">…</MarkerList>

## PasswordStrength (forms)
Password-strength indicator: a segmented meter + label, with an optional requirements checklist. Scoring-agnostic — controlled score, a custom estimate function, or a built-in length/character-class heuristic.
Props:
- value: string — Password to score via the built-in heuristic or `estimate`. Ignored when `score` is set.
- score: number — Controlled strength level index (0..levels-1; -1 = empty/too-short). Takes precedence over value/estimate.
- estimate: (value: string) => number — Custom scorer over `value` returning a level index (e.g. wrap zxcvbn). Falls back to the built-in heuristic.
- levels: number (default: 4) — Number of strength levels/segments. Match your estimator (e.g. 5 for zxcvbn 0–4); labels.levels length should match.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Meter size
- showLabel: boolean (default: true) — Show the strength text label beneath the meter
- labels: Partial<PasswordStrengthLabels> — Level names, empty-state text, and the aria-live announcement prefix
- id: string — Element id (lets a password field point aria-describedby at the meter)
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Optional PasswordStrength.Requirements rendered beneath the meter
PasswordStrength.Requirements props:
- requirements: { label: string; met: boolean }[] — Rules to display; the consumer computes `met` (keeps the component scoring-agnostic)
- labels: Partial<PasswordStrengthLabels> — Accessible labels for the met / not-met states (met, unmet)
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
Example: <PasswordStrength>…</PasswordStrength>

## Select (forms)
Dropdown select built on Radix Select — a combobox trigger, listbox popup with option items, and a hidden native <select> for form submission — with an animated popup and item stagger

- defaultOpen: boolean — Default open state (uncontrolled)

- invalid: boolean — Invalid state

- width: 'auto' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' (default: full) — How wide the trigger is, from the field-width scale. Steps are sized in ch for the content each expects, and every one is capped at the space available. 'full' takes the column, 'auto' hugs the content.
- minWidth: Dimension — Minimum width override (token default: 10rem)
- maxWidth: Dimension — Maximum width override (token default: 30rem — prevents absurdly wide selects in stretched parents)

- className: string — CSS class name

- children: React.ReactNode — Custom icon content (defaults to chevron-down)
Select.Content props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Content children (Viewport, Items, etc.)
- sideOffset: number (default: 4) — Distance from trigger in px
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' — Alignment along the trigger axis
- container: HTMLElement — Custom portal mount target. Defaults to document.body.
- width: 'anchor' | 'content' (default: anchor) — Where the popover takes its width from. 'anchor' matches the trigger, so trigger and list read as one control; 'content' sizes to the widest option and stays inside the room the anchor has.
- minWidth: Dimension — Minimum width override (token default: 10rem)
- maxWidth: Dimension — Maximum width override (token default: 30rem)
- onPointerDownOutside: (e: Event) => void — Pointer down outside handler
- onEscapeKeyDown: (e: KeyboardEvent) => void — Escape key handler

- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Items and groups

## Skeleton (feedback)
Compound placeholder shapes for loading states with pulse and wave animation modes
Skeleton.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Shape sub-components to render
- loading: boolean (default: true) — Whether to render skeleton (returns null when false)
- animation: 'pulse' | 'wave' | false (default: pulse) — Animation style: pulse fades opacity, wave sweeps a highlight gradient
Skeleton.Circle props:
- diameter: Dimension (default: 40) — Circle diameter. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length. Named `diameter` rather than `size` because `size` is the scale token everywhere else in the library.
Skeleton.Rectangle props:
- width: Dimension (default: 100%) — Rectangle width
- height: Dimension (default: 1rem) — Rectangle height
Skeleton.Rounded props:
- width: Dimension (default: 100%) — Width of the rounded shape
- height: Dimension (default: 1rem) — Height of the rounded shape
- radius: string (default: var(--move-skeleton-radius)) — Border radius value
Skeleton.Text props:
- lines: number (default: 3) — Number of text lines to render
- spacing: string (default: var(--move-skeleton-text-spacing)) — Gap between lines
- lineHeight: string (default: var(--move-skeleton-text-line-height)) — Height of each line
- lastLineWidth: string (default: 60%) — Width of the last line (shorter for realism)
Example: <Skeleton.Root>…</Skeleton.Root>

## Splitter (layout)
Resizable panel layout with draggable gutters, keyboard resize support, and responsive collapse to vertical stacking
Splitter.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Panel children (gutters are injected automatically between them)
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- layout: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' (default: horizontal) — Layout direction of the panels
- gutterSize: number (default: 4) — Size of the gutter/handle in pixels
- collapseBelow: number — Container width in pixels below which horizontal layout collapses to vertical stacking
- fill: 'remaining' — Where the Root's height comes from. It already fills its parent (100%); set 'remaining' when it sits in a flex chain and should take the space left after siblings. See /systems/layout.
- onResizeEnd: (sizes: number[]) => void — Callback fired when panel resize completes, with current sizes as percentages
Splitter.Panel props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Panel content
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- defaultSize: Dimension — Starting size before the user drags. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length or percentage. Applies along the Splitter's axis — width when horizontal, height when vertical. Omit it and the panel takes an equal share of what its sized siblings leave.
- minSize: Dimension (default: 44) — Smallest the panel can be dragged to. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length or percentage. Applies along the Splitter's axis — width when horizontal, height when vertical. Defaults to 44px (WCAG 2.5.8 enhanced target size), which unlike a percentage means the same thing in both orientations and at every window size.
Example: <Splitter.Root>…</Splitter.Root>

## Stack (layout)
Flex layout container for vertical or horizontal stacking with configurable gap, alignment, and responsive collapse
Props:
- direction: 'row' | 'column' (default: column) — Flex direction
- gap: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'none' (default: md) — Gap between children
- padding: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | '3xl' | 'none' — Padding around the stack. One token for all sides, or a two-value "block inline" shorthand like CSS (e.g. "md 2xl" — top/bottom md, left/right 2xl). Uses the extended scale (adds 2xl/3xl) since stacks frequently sit at page-level scope.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch' | 'baseline' (default: stretch) — Cross-axis alignment (align-items)
- justify: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'between' | 'evenly' (default: start) — Main-axis alignment (justify-content)
- wrap: boolean (default: false) — Allow children to wrap to next line
- collapseBelow: string — Container width threshold (px) below which direction collapses to column
- flex: 1 | 'auto' | 'none' — Flex sizing along the parent's main axis. 1 = grow to fill remaining space (with min-width:0 so wide children scroll instead of overflowing the row); 'auto' = size to content but allow grow/shrink; 'none' = fixed at content size.
- fill: 'parent' | 'remaining' — Where this box's height comes from. 'parent' = all of the parent's height (the parent must be sized, and you must be its only child or you overflow it); 'remaining' = the space left after siblings, waiving the automatic minimum size so a scroll region below can actually scroll. Prefer 'remaining'. Neither knows what a viewport is — that enters at the app boundary via <MoveRoot fullHeight>. See /systems/layout.
- clip: boolean — Clip overflowing content (overflow: clip) — a boundary, not a scroller. Deliberately not overflow:hidden, which stays programmatically scrollable and lets a focused child silently scroll the box with no scrollbar to return by. To scroll, use ScrollArea.
- stagger: boolean | { delay?: number; from?: 'first' | 'last' | 'center' } (default: false) — Opt-in: reveal direct children with a staggered fade+rise entrance on mount. `true` uses defaults (60ms between items, from first); pass an object to tune `delay`/`from`. Off by default — when unset, Stack renders with no animation. Disable or override via the `animations` prop.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Override or disable the entrance stagger animation (only relevant when `stagger` is set).
- children: React.ReactNode — Child elements to lay out
Example: <Stack direction="column" gap="md">…</Stack>

## Table (data-display)
Compound tabular data primitive. Variants for the frame (surface / lines / bordered), a striped modifier, a responsive mode (scroll default, stack below breakpoint), and a Group/GroupHeader compound for collapsible row groups.
Props:
- variant: 'surface' | 'lines' | 'bordered' | 'ghost' (default: lines) — Visual frame variant.
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Cell padding and font size.
- striped: boolean — Zebra-stripe body rows.
- hoverable: boolean — Tint rows on hover.
- stickyHeader: boolean — Stick the header on scroll.
- responsive: 'scroll' | 'stack' | 'none' (default: scroll) — Responsive strategy.
- stackBelow: number (default: 640) — Stack-mode container breakpoint in px.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Row entrance animation config or false.
- children: React.ReactNode — Table sections.
Table.Root props:
- variant: 'surface' | 'lines' | 'bordered' | 'ghost' (default: lines) — Visual frame: borderless with horizontal rules (lines, default), card-like (surface), full grid (bordered), or no chrome at all (ghost — use with `striped` for zebra-only).
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Cell padding and font size.
- striped: boolean — Zebra-stripe even rows in the body. Composes with any variant.
- hoverable: boolean — Tint rows on hover.
- stickyHeader: boolean — Stick the header to the top while the body scrolls.
- responsive: 'scroll' | 'stack' | 'none' (default: scroll) — Responsive strategy: overflow-x scroll (default), flip to stacked cards below stackBelow, or none.
- stackBelow: number (default: 640) — Container-width breakpoint in pixels below which stack mode activates. Only used when responsive="stack".
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Staggered row entrance animation config or false to disable.
- children: React.ReactNode — Table sections (Header, Body, Footer, Group).
Table.Header props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Header rows. Text inside Head cells is used as labels for stack mode.
Table.Body props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Body rows.
Table.Footer props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Footer rows.
Table.Row props:
- selected: boolean — Mark row as selected.
- valign: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' — Vertical alignment of this row's cells (start = top, center = middle, end = bottom). Defaults to the browser's middle; start keeps neighbours aligned when one cell is multi-line.
- interactive: boolean — Make the row a click target. Adds cursor, hover tint, focus ring, and Enter/Space activation.
- onClick: (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLTableRowElement>) => void — Row click handler.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Row-level hover animation config or false to disable.
- children: React.ReactNode — Row cells.
Table.Head props:
- sortable: boolean — Enable sort interaction on this column.
- sorted: 'asc' | 'desc' | false — Current sort direction or false.
- onSort: () => void — Callback when sort is triggered.
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' — Column alignment for the header label.
- children: React.ReactNode — Header cell content.
Table.Cell props:
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' — Cell alignment.
- description: React.ReactNode — When set, the cell renders its children as a bold primary line with this muted description below.
- children: React.ReactNode — Cell content.
Table.Caption props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Caption text.
Table.Group props:
- collapsible: boolean (default: true) — When false, the group renders as a static section — header has no chevron and is not clickable.
- open: boolean — Controlled open state.
- defaultOpen: boolean (default: true) — Initial open state when uncontrolled.
- onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void — Fires when the open state changes.
- children: React.ReactNode — GroupHeader followed by Rows.
Table.GroupHeader props:
- colSpan: number — Number of columns the header spans. Inferred from Table.Header column count by default.
- children: React.ReactNode — Group label.
Example: <Table variant="lines" responsive="scroll">…</Table>

## TableOfContents (navigation)
Right-rail table of contents with scroll-spy active-state tracking, indented nesting, and smooth-scroll anchor navigation.
TableOfContents.Root props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — TableOfContents.Item elements
- offset: number (default: 80) — Top-of-viewport offset (in px) used to decide which heading is current
- labels: Partial<TableOfContentsLabels> — Override accessible label strings
TableOfContents.Item props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Item label
- href: string — Anchor href — e.g. "#section-id"
- depth: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 (default: 1) — Nesting level; visually indents the item
Example: <TableOfContents.Root>…</TableOfContents.Root>

## Tabs (navigation)
Tabbed interface with underline/pills/outline variants, sliding indicator animation, and Radix Tabs primitive
Tabs.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Tab list and content elements
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- defaultValue: string — Initial active tab value (uncontrolled)
- value: string — Controlled active tab value
- onValueChange: (value: string) => void — Called when active tab changes
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' — Orientation of tab list
- dir: 'ltr' | 'rtl' — Text direction for keyboard navigation
- activationMode: 'automatic' | 'manual' — Whether tabs activate on focus (automatic) or on click (manual)
Tabs.List props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Tab trigger elements
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- loop: boolean — Whether keyboard navigation loops around
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Tab size affecting padding and font size
- variant: 'underline' | 'pills' | 'outline' (default: underline) — Visual style variant
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Pass false to disable sliding indicator animation
Tabs.Trigger props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Tab label content
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- value: string — Unique value associating trigger with content
- disabled: boolean — Disable the tab trigger
Tabs.Content props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Panel content
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- value: string — Value matching the trigger to show this content
- forceMount: true — Force mount content even when inactive
Example: <Tabs.Root>…</Tabs.Root>

## Text (typography)
Typography primitive with configurable element, size, weight, color, alignment, and truncation
Props:
- as: 'p' | 'span' | 'div' | 'em' | 'strong' | 'small' | 'del' (default: p) — HTML element to render as
- size: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'base' | 'lg' | 'xl' (default: base) — Font size
- weight: 'normal' | 'medium' | 'semibold' | 'bold' (default: normal) — Font weight
- color: 'base' | 'muted' | 'subtle' | 'primary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' (default: base) — Text color
- align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' — Text alignment (optional)
- truncate: Truncate — Truncate overflowing text: true/'end', 'start', or 'clamp'
- lines: number — Max lines for truncate='clamp' (default 2)
- tooltip: boolean — With truncate, show full text in a Move Tooltip when actually cut off
- readableWidth: boolean — Cap the line length to a comfortable reading measure (WCAG 1.4.8) for a standalone paragraph — use Prose for real long-form content
- children: React.ReactNode — Text content
Example: <Text as="p" weight="normal">…</Text>

## Textarea (forms)
Multi-line text input with outlined/filled variants, auto-resize support, and configurable size
Props:
- variant: 'outlined' | 'filled' (default: outlined) — Visual style variant
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Size controlling padding and font size
- invalid: boolean — Whether the textarea is in an invalid/error state
- autoSize: boolean — Automatically adjust height based on content
- minRows: number — Minimum number of visible rows when autoSize is enabled
- maxRows: number — Maximum number of visible rows when autoSize is enabled
- rows: number (default: 3) — Number of visible text rows
- resize: 'none' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal' | 'both' (default: vertical) — CSS resize behavior (overridden to none when autoSize is true)
- width: 'auto' | 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'full' (default: full) — How wide the field is, from the field-width scale. Steps are sized in ch for the content each expects, and every one is capped at the space available. 'full' takes the column.
- disabled: boolean — Whether the textarea is disabled
- readOnly: boolean — Whether the textarea is read-only
- placeholder: string — Placeholder text
- value: string — Controlled textarea value
- defaultValue: string — Uncontrolled default textarea value
- name: string — Form submission name
- id: string — Element id for label association
- required: boolean — Whether the textarea is required
- autoFocus: boolean — Whether to auto-focus on mount
- onChange: React.ChangeEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement> — Change event handler
- onFocus: React.FocusEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement> — Focus event handler
- onBlur: React.FocusEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement> — Blur event handler
- onKeyDown: React.KeyboardEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement> — Keydown event handler
Example: <Textarea variant="outlined" resize="vertical">…</Textarea>

## TimeField (date-time)
Time input with individual hour/minute/second segments, optional 12h/24h cycle, and dropdown column picker
Props:
- value: string — Controlled time value
- defaultValue: string — Default time value
- onValueChange: (value: string) => void — Value change handler
- granularity: 'hour' | 'minute' | 'second' (default: minute) — Visible segments
- hourCycle: 12 | 24 (default: 24) — Hour display cycle
- withDropdown: boolean (default: false) — Enable dropdown picker
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Dropdown animation config
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Input size
- disabled: boolean (default: false) — Disabled state
- invalid: boolean (default: false) — Invalid state
- min: string — Min time constraint
- max: string — Max time constraint
- step: number (default: 1) — Increment step
- labels: Partial<TimeFieldLabels> — Override aria-label strings for segments and period
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom segment layout
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
TimeField.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Custom segment layout or auto-rendered segments
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- value: string — Controlled time value in 24h format (HH, HH:mm, HH:mm:ss)
- defaultValue: string — Default time value (uncontrolled)
- onValueChange: (value: string) => void — Called when time value changes
- granularity: 'hour' | 'minute' | 'second' (default: minute) — Which segments to show
- hourCycle: 12 | 24 (default: 24) — 12 or 24 hour display cycle
- withDropdown: boolean (default: false) — Show dropdown column picker on ArrowDown
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config for dropdown enter/exit
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Input size
- disabled: boolean (default: false) — Disabled state
- invalid: boolean (default: false) — Invalid state
- min: string — Minimum time constraint (24h format)
- max: string — Maximum time constraint (24h format)
- step: number (default: 1) — Arrow key increment in seconds
- labels: Partial<TimeFieldLabels> — Override aria-label strings for segments and period
TimeField.Segment props:
- segment: SegmentType — Which segment this renders (hour, minute, second)
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
TimeField.Separator props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode (default: :) — Separator content
TimeField.Period props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
TimeField.Dropdown props:
- children: React.ReactNode — DropdownColumn elements
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
TimeField.DropdownColumn props:
- segment: SegmentType | 'period' — Which segment this column represents
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
Example: <TimeField granularity="minute">…</TimeField>

## Timeline (data-display)
Vertical timeline with progress tracking, custom bullets, color-coded states, alternate alignment, and staggered entrance animation
Props:
- active: number (default: -1) — Index of the active step
- align: 'left' | 'right' | 'alternate' (default: left) — Content alignment
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Timeline size
- color: 'gray' | 'red' | 'pink' | 'grape' | 'violet' | 'indigo' | 'blue' | 'cyan' | 'teal' | 'green' | 'lime' | 'yellow' | 'orange' (default: indigo) — Default color for active/completed items
- lineVariant: 'solid' | 'dashed' | 'dotted' (default: solid) — Line style for connectors
- reverseActive: boolean (default: false) — Reverse active direction
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Staggered entrance animation config or false to disable
- children: React.ReactNode — Timeline.Item children
Timeline.Root props:
- active: number (default: -1) — Index of the active step (-1 for all inactive)
- align: 'left' | 'right' | 'alternate' (default: left) — Content alignment relative to the timeline line
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Timeline size affecting bullet, line width, and spacing
- color: 'gray' | 'red' | 'pink' | 'grape' | 'violet' | 'indigo' | 'blue' | 'cyan' | 'teal' | 'green' | 'lime' | 'yellow' | 'orange' (default: indigo) — Default color for active/completed items
- lineVariant: 'solid' | 'dashed' | 'dotted' (default: solid) — Line style for connectors
- reverseActive: boolean (default: false) — Reverse active direction (items after active index are completed)
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Staggered entrance animation config or false to disable
- children: React.ReactNode — Timeline.Item children
Timeline.Item props:
- bullet: React.ReactNode — Custom bullet content (icon, avatar, etc.)
- title: React.ReactNode — Item title text
- lineVariant: 'solid' | 'dashed' | 'dotted' — Override line variant for this item
- color: 'gray' | 'red' | 'pink' | 'grape' | 'violet' | 'indigo' | 'blue' | 'cyan' | 'teal' | 'green' | 'lime' | 'yellow' | 'orange' — Override color for this item
- children: React.ReactNode — Item body content
Example: <Timeline align="left" color="indigo">…</Timeline>

## ToggleGroup (actions)
Segmented control with sliding indicator that allows single selection among a set of toggle items, using Radix ToggleGroup primitive
ToggleGroup.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — ToggleGroup.Item elements
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- value: string — Controlled selected item value
- defaultValue: string — Initial selected item value (uncontrolled)
- onValueChange: (value: string) => void — Called when selection changes
- orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' (default: horizontal) — Layout orientation
- disabled: boolean — Disable the entire group
- loop: boolean (default: true) — Whether keyboard navigation loops around
- size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: md) — Item size affecting padding and font size
- variant: 'pills' | 'underline' | 'outline' (default: pills) — Visual appearance, shared with Tabs: a filled sliding pill, a Pinterest-style underline filter bar, or connected outlined segments. Inherited by items.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Pass false to disable indicator animation
ToggleGroup.Item props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Item label content
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- value: string — Unique value for this item
- disabled: boolean — Disable this specific item
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Per-item animation overrides; defaults to no animation to avoid scale artifacts on connected items
Example: <ToggleGroup.Root>…</ToggleGroup.Root>

## Tooltip (overlays)
Floating label that appears on hover/focus to describe an element, with spring entrance and direction-aware positioning
Props:
- label: React.ReactNode — Tooltip text content
- children: React.ReactElement — Trigger element (rendered via asChild)
- side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' (default: top) — Preferred placement side
- sideOffset: number (default: 4) — Distance from trigger in px
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' — Alignment along the side axis
- arrow: boolean (default: true) — Show arrow pointing to trigger
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config or false to disable
- delayDuration: number — Delay before tooltip opens (ms)
- open: boolean — Controlled open state
- defaultOpen: boolean — Initial open state (uncontrolled) — opens on mount, hover-driven thereafter
- onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void — Called when open state changes
Tooltip.Provider props:
- children: React.ReactNode — App or section content
- delayDuration: number — Delay before first tooltip opens (ms)
- skipDelayDuration: number — Delay before subsequent tooltips open (ms)
- disableHoverableContent: boolean — Prevent tooltip content from staying open on hover
Tooltip.Root props:
- children: React.ReactNode — Trigger and content elements
- open: boolean — Controlled open state
- defaultOpen: boolean — Initial open state (uncontrolled)
- onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void — Called when open state changes
- delayDuration: number — Delay before tooltip opens (ms)
- disableHoverableContent: boolean — Prevent content from staying open on hover
Tooltip.Trigger props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Trigger content
- asChild: boolean — Merge props onto child element instead of wrapping
Tooltip.Content props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- children: React.ReactNode — Tooltip content
- side: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' (default: top) — Preferred side relative to trigger
- sideOffset: number — Distance from trigger in px
- align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' (default: center) — Alignment along the side axis
- alignOffset: number — Alignment offset in px
- container: HTMLElement — Custom portal mount target. Defaults to document.body.
- animations: AnimationTrigger[] | false — Animation config or false to disable
Tooltip.Arrow props:
- className: string — CSS class name
- style: React.CSSProperties — Inline styles
- width: Dimension — Arrow width in px
- height: Dimension — Arrow height in px
Example: <Tooltip side="top" align="start">…</Tooltip>

## VideoPlayer (media)
Custom HTML5 video player with glassmorphism controls bar, progress scrubbing, volume, subtitles, playback speed, quality switching, fullscreen, and auto-hiding controls
Props:
- src: string — Video source URL
- poster: string — Poster image URL shown before playback
- provider: VideoPlayerProvider — Custom media provider (e.g. HLS.js adapter) with setup/destroy lifecycle
- subtitles: SubtitleTrack[] — Array of subtitle/caption tracks (VTT files)
- autoPlay: boolean — Start playback automatically
- muted: boolean — Start muted
- loop: boolean — Loop playback
- playbackRate: number — Controlled playback speed
- onPlaybackRateChange: (rate: number) => void — Called when playback rate changes
- playing: boolean — Controlled playing state
- onPlayingChange: (playing: boolean) => void — Called when playing state changes
- volume: number — Controlled volume (0-1)
- onVolumeChange: (volume: number) => void — Called when volume changes
- currentTime: number — Controlled current playback time in seconds
- onTimeChange: (time: number) => void — Called when current time changes
- onEnded: () => void — Called when playback ends
- onError: (error: MediaError | null) => void — Called on playback error
- onReady: () => void — Called when video metadata is loaded and ready
- qualities: QualityOption[] — Array of quality options for source switching
- audioTracks: AudioTrack[] — Array of audio track options for source switching
- onQualityChange: (quality: QualityOption) => void — Called when quality is changed
- onAudioTrackChange: (track: AudioTrack) => void — Called when audio track is changed
- showSettings: boolean (default: true) — Show the settings menu button
- showVolume: boolean (default: true) — Show volume button and slider
- showSubtitles: boolean (default: true) — Show the subtitles menu button (only if subtitles are provided)
- showFullscreen: boolean (default: true) — Show the fullscreen toggle button
- showTime: boolean (default: true) — Show the time display
- labels: Partial<VideoPlayerLabels> — i18n labels for the player controls
- radius: 'none' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' (default: none) — Border radius of the player container
- aspectRatio: string — CSS aspect-ratio value applied to the root
- width: Dimension — Width of the player (number treated as px)
- height: Dimension — Height of the player (number treated as px)
- children: React.ReactNode — Additional content rendered inside the player container
Example: <VideoPlayer radius="none">…</VideoPlayer>
